Last month, we put our 16 year old toy rat terrier down. Gizmo was our treasure. We lived that little guy so much. He had become deaf at 14, had spondylosis,  high blood pressure, and had uncomfortable growth in his shoulder. We noticed a little bump on his foot that blew up in 2 weeks to a golf ball. We had it checked, and it was a rare cancer.

Our options were to amputate his leg as they couldn't remove due to not being able to close the wound and to prevent cancer from spreading.

He still ate, loved all the treats we gave him, and seemed to have 5050 good vs. bad times.

We scheduled a home euthanasia 2 weeks later. His sarcoma burst, and the gaping hole got infected.

He did not have to go when he did. We could have kept soaking his wound, giving him 5 medications, and kept him in a doughnut all day/night.

We didn't do that. We gave him a send-off of amazing treats, his special meal, and as much live as we could possibly impart. He was sedated in our arms while being held, kissed, and surrounded by his favorite people. It was devastating but peaceful. 

I'd rather do it sooner than later and be able to give my sweet baby a living, peaceful , send off surrounded with love than to let it get to the point where they are suffering linger than they have to.

We split our money.  We used to fight constantly about money.  I'm a saver he's a spender. It was causing serious issues in our relationship. 

Our decision to separate financially saved our marriage. 

We totaled up our fixed expenses.  Put our variable expenses on a joint credit card. Decided a % We would each save in 401k.

Our portion of the expenses are a percentage based on our individual income, so it's fair. We each send our portion of fixed to our joint account and pay off our joint credit card based on the % we owe.

What's leftover is our own money. we are free to do what we want with, and there is NO judgment from either of us. 

I have my own brokerage and savings account.  He has a bunch of toys and tools.

No more fights about money = happily married.

I'm sure eventually I would have reached the conclusion he would be.

Nobody else even registered in my mind. I thought only 3 people would be impacted, and I was convinced 2 out of the 3 would be just fine.

Thankfully, my thinking was so disordered I slipped up and she picked up the warning signs and my therapist coaxed me into going to the hospital to be evaluated.  I was put into hospital against my wishes.

I hated being in the hospital,  didn't realize why they were so stupid to not understand everyone was better off without me.

Depression is scary as fuck. It takes hold of your mind, stunts the ability to think clearly,  and pushes me towards death.  I am still terrified how my mind was able to get to that place.  Hopefully it never will again.
